title: Live In Vivo Imaging and Analysis of GCaMP6F
author: Bryan Yoo
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bzp7p5rn
materials: The proximal colon was identified, and this portion was placed on top of a stack of 4-6 glass microscopy slides (depending on size of animal) (VWR, Radnor PA-Cat. No. 48300-026).

steps.title: Deliver AAV-PHP.S-CAG-GCaMP6F
steps.instruction: Systemically deliver 10^12 VGs of AAV-PHP.S-CAG-GCaMP6F to WT C57 mice.

steps.title: Anesthetize Mice
steps.instruction: 3-4 weeks after infection, anesthetize mice using 2% isoflurane on a heating pad (Kent Scientific, Torrington, CT-DCT15) with plastic sleeve covers (Kent Scientific, Torrington, CT-DCT1520P).

steps.title: Expose Intestines
steps.instruction: Surgically open the abdominal cavity to expose the intestines.

steps.title: Secure Tissue for Imaging
steps.instruction: Secure the tissue onto a glass slide using a glass coverslip and a biorthogonal silicon elastomer (Kwik-Sil) (World Precision Instruments, Sarasota, FL-KWIK-SIL).

substeps.instruction: Hold the coverslip steadily to ensure a flat imaging surface, as the elastomer stiffens within 1 minute of application.

steps.title: Perform Confocal Imaging
steps.instruction: Place the anesthetized mouse under an upright confocal microscope (Zeiss LSM 880) and capture GCaMP6F fluorescence.

substeps.instruction: Set imaging frequency to 5Hz (1 image every 200ms).

steps.title: Analyze Fluorescence and Track Cells
steps.instruction: Perform 2D cell tracking and record fluorescence intensity from cells.

substeps.instruction: Use the TrackMate ImageJ plugin (https://imagej.net/TrackMate) for cell tracking.
